samples.summary: A third, un-updated copy of the session-limit regex survives in metrics.mjs and has now drifted from the widened `SESSION_LIMIT_RE`
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/metrics.mjs:878 — `const sessionLimited = outcome.code ? outcome.code === "USAGE_LIMIT" : /\b(?:session|usage)\s+limit\b/i.test(detail);`. The diff's whole rationale is that two copies of this pattern drifted; this third copy was not imported or widened. For any fix-run outcome without `code` (the pre-vocabulary/persisted-log fallback the comment at metrics.mjs:876-877 explicitly keeps alive), a `weekly`/`daily`/`monthly limit` now renders the wrong maintainer advice ("a human should take a look" instead of "wait for the window to reset"), while ask.mjs/redact.mjs/auth-smoke.mjs all treat it as a usage window. Fix belongs here: import `SESSION_LIMIT_RE` from redact.mjs.

samples.summary: `isCredentialRejected` keys on `AUTH_REJECTED` only, so a slot classified `AUTH_MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL` still kills the whole run with healthy credentials unused
samples.evidence: redact.mjs:390 returns `AUTH_MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL` (it outranks the status check, so such an error carries that code and typically no status), and redact.mjs:250 documents it as a per-credential fault whose remedy is rotating that secret. `isCredentialRejected` (scripts/agent/ask.mjs:600-605) returns `false` for it because the `code` branch short-circuits before the 401/403 status fallback, so `nextCredential` (ask.mjs:639) will not fail over — exactly the per-slot fault (one env slot with a stray newline/whitespace) that this change exists to route around. Confirming needs a run where a pool slot is malformed rather than merely expired.

samples.summary: Swapping the literal `/session limit/i` and `/usage limit/i` for the anchored `SESSION_LIMIT_RE` narrows the smoke test: plural phrasings no longer classify as quota
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/auth-smoke.mjs:51 now uses `/\b(?:session|usage|weekly|daily|monthly)\s+limit\b/i`. The trailing `\b` means text such as "you've hit your usage limits" or "session limits reached" — matched by the previous unanchored `/usage limit/i` at auth-smoke.mjs (old line 50) — no longer matches any QUOTA entry, falls through to AUTH or `unknown` (classifyFailure, auth-smoke.mjs:84-86) and exits 1, which is precisely the auth/quota misdiagnosis the header at auth-smoke.mjs:39-44 warns against. Needs a sample of the upstream's plural phrasing to confirm reachability.

samples.summary: Top-level design doc still states the pool replaces a credential only when that account's usage window closes
samples.evidence: docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1923-1924 — "and replaces it only when that account's window closes". After this change `nextCredential` also retires a slot on `AUTH_REJECTED`/401/403 (scripts/agent/ask.mjs:639), so the documented pool contract is now wrong; the link-check lane only validates backticked paths, so nothing catches this.

samples.summary: `isExhausted`'s docblock in token-pool.mjs still explains drained as "every account's window is closed", the wording ask.mjs deliberately abandoned
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/token-pool.mjs:152-155: "A DRAINED pool returning null means every account's window is closed". The diff changed the operator-facing message in ask.mjs:693 to "was retired" precisely because a slot can now be retired for a refused credential too; this out-of-diff docblock (and `advance`'s comment at token-pool.mjs:164-167, which describes reports as hitting "the same closed window") still asserts the single-cause reading.

finding.summary: `isCredentialRejected` keys on `AUTH_REJECTED` only, so a slot classified `AUTH_MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL` still kills the whole run with healthy credentials unused
finding.evidence: redact.mjs:390 returns `AUTH_MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL` (it outranks the status check, so such an error carries that code and typically no status), and redact.mjs:250 documents it as a per-credential fault whose remedy is rotating that secret. `isCredentialRejected` (scripts/agent/ask.mjs:600-605) returns `false` for it because the `code` branch short-circuits before the 401/403 status fallback, so `nextCredential` (ask.mjs:639) will not fail over — exactly the per-slot fault (one env slot with a stray newline/whitespace) that this change exists to route around. Confirming needs a run where a pool slot is malformed rather than merely expired.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. ask.mjs:602 short-circuits on `err.code`, returning true only for AUTH_REJECTED, so an error carrying AUTH_MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL never reaches the 401/403 fallback at ask.mjs:603-604. That code is reachable on the live path: classifyInfraError tests MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL_RE before the status branch (redact.mjs:387-390, outranking the 401→AUTH_REJECTED rule at redact.mjs:400), classifyResult folds it in via safeFailure (ask.mjs:322-329, 378-386), and runSession stamps it onto the thrown error as `err.code` (ask.mjs:788); ask.test.mjs:651-659 shows the real incident string producing exactly that shape. nextCredential (ask.mjs:639) therefore returns null and askStructured rethrows at ask.mjs:718 without calling pool.advance — the run dies with healthy pool slots unused. I searched for a counterexample and found none: `pool.advance(` has exactly one caller repo-wide (ask.mjs:640), no other module consumes AUTH_MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL for a failover decision, and the only upstream mitigation — token-pool.mjs:57 `.trim()` — strips only leading/trailing whitespace, whereas the documented fault (redact.mjs:3-14, fixture ask.test.mjs:650) is a space embedded inside the token. auth-smoke.mjs:60-76 classifies malformed secrets but is a pre-flight check outside the failover loop. In lane as a reachable per-slot-fault path that bypasses the new failover contract between redact.mjs's closed vocabulary and ask.mjs's predicate.
